CandidateDrug.description: One ranked candidate drug for a ``DiseaseQuery``.
CandidateDrug.title: CandidateDrug

CandidateScore.description:
One scoring method's verdict on a candidate -- a disease-based
evaluation may report several (path quality, popularity, a future
TransE score), never collapsed into one undifferentiated number.
CandidateScore.title: CandidateScore

completion_date.description: statusModule.completionDateStruct.date, copied as reported -- not reformatted
completion_date.title: Completion Date

source_id.description: the source's own identifier, e.g. a PMID or NCT number -- never fabricated
source_id.title: Source Id

start_date.description: statusModule.startDateStruct.date, copied as reported -- not reformatted
start_date.title: Start Date

study_type.description: ClinicalTrials.gov's own designModule.studyType, copied as reported
study_type.title: Study Type

DiseaseBiologyModule.description:
What Open Targets reports for one disease: its own description,
plus the targets most strongly associated with it, ranked by genetic
evidence. ``total_associated_targets`` is Open Targets' total match
count, independent of how many are returned in ``targets``.
DiseaseBiologyModule.title: DiseaseBiologyModule

DiseaseBiologyQuery.description:
A request to look up the disease-biology module for one disease.
Exactly one of ``disease_name``/``disease_id`` should be given --
``disease_name`` is resolved to an Open Targets ID first (see
``DiseaseBiologyResponse.resolved_from``); ``disease_id`` (an EFO or
MONDO ID) skips that resolution step.
DiseaseBiologyQuery.title: DiseaseBiologyQuery

DiseaseBiologyResponse.description:
What ``POST /api/v1/disease-biology`` returns. ``resolved_from`` is
set only when ``disease_name`` was given and had to be resolved to an
Open Targets ID first -- it lists the top candidate matches Open
Targets' own search returned, so a caller can see what else the name
could have meant, not just the one picked.

disclaimer.default: Research evidence integration from Open Targets. Association with a gene is not a causal claim.
disclaimer.title: Disclaimer

DiseaseBiologyResponse.title: DiseaseBiologyResponse

DiseaseMatch.description:
One candidate disease returned when resolving a free-text name to
an Open Targets disease ID (EFO or MONDO).

search_score.description: Open Targets' own search relevance score, not a biological score
search_score.title: Search Score

DiseaseMatch.title: DiseaseMatch

DiseaseQuery.description:
A request to rank candidate drugs for one disease. Exactly one of
``disease_name``/``disease_id`` should be given -- the same
name-or-canonical-ID convention already used by the CLI's
``rank-drugs`` command.
DiseaseQuery.title: DiseaseQuery

EvidenceBundle.description:
All evidence gathered so far for one candidate drug/disease pair.
Every list defaults empty -- an empty bundle means "no lookups have
been run yet", never "no evidence exists".
EvidenceBundle.title: EvidenceBundle

EvidenceLookupResponse.description:
What ``POST /api/v1/evidence`` returns: one live, synchronous lookup
across PubMed, ClinicalTrials.gov, openFDA and DailyMed (see that
router's docstring for why this is synchronous for now). ``bundle`` is
the same ``EvidenceBundle`` the evidence domain already defines --
presence of a record here is not a claim of efficacy or safety.

disclaimer.default: Research evidence lookup. Presence of a record is not proof of efficacy or safety.
disclaimer.title: Disclaimer

EvidenceLookupResponse.title: EvidenceLookupResponse

EvidenceQuery.description: A request to look up real external evidence for one drug/disease pair.
EvidenceQuery.title: EvidenceQuery

EvidenceSource.description:
Where a piece of evidence would come from. Matches the sources
named in the project README's "Planned" section.
EvidenceSource.title: EvidenceSource

EvidenceStrength.description:
A coarse, non-clinical categorization of evidence type -- never a
claim about whether the evidence shows efficacy.
EvidenceStrength.title: EvidenceStrength

EvidenceSummary.description:
One piece of graph evidence linking a candidate drug toward a
disease -- a relation type and the node types it connects, not a path
in full (see ``ExplanationPath`` for that).
EvidenceSummary.title: EvidenceSummary

ExplanationPath.description:
A full mechanistic path from drug to disease, as the CLI's
``explain-paths``/``rank-drugs`` commands already compute -- a
hypothesis to review, not evidence of efficacy. Graph connectivity
between a drug and a disease is not itself evidence of efficacy, and
``path_score`` (when present) is the heuristic defined in
``repurposemap.scoring.path_quality``, not a probability or a model
confidence.
ExplanationPath.title: ExplanationPath

ExplanationStep.description:
One hop of an explanation path, mirroring
``repurposemap.graph.paths.PathStep``'s own representation -- source
and target node *type* (e.g. "drug", "gene/protein", "disease") is
carried through unchanged, never inferred or guessed here.
ExplanationStep.title: ExplanationStep

HealthResponse.description:
What ``GET /health`` returns. Deliberately static -- no graph load,
no model check, just "is the process up and which API version is this".
HealthResponse.title: HealthResponse

ModelProvenanceInfo.description:
What the experiment/model provenance layer
(``repurposemap.provenance``) can safely report about model status --
read from approved ``ml/experiments/*.json`` files only, never a
checkpoint tensor, never a locked-test label.

inference_eligible.description: whether an eligible final-training experiment record exists AND a checkpoint is explicitly configured
inference_eligible.title: Inference Eligible

most_recent_completed_stage.description: stage name of the most recently generated valid experiment record
most_recent_completed_stage.title: Most Recent Completed Stage

ModelProvenanceInfo.title: ModelProvenanceInfo

ModelStatus.description:
Whether a real ranking model is configured. ``available=False`` is
the honest default until a specific, eligible model is explicitly
supplied -- never guessed, never silently assumed.

model_type.description: e.g. 'path-quality', 'transe' -- None until a model is configured
model_type.title: Model Type

ModelStatus.title: ModelStatus

Pathway.description: One Reactome pathway a target participates in.
Pathway.title: Pathway

Provenance.description:
Dataset/source provenance -- only fields knowable without touching
the raw file (see ``repurposemap.adapters.primekg.PrimeKGFingerprint``,
whose ``sha256``/``size_bytes`` require reading the file and are
deliberately NOT surfaced here).
Provenance.title: Provenance

publication_types.description: PubMed's own publication-type labels (e.g. 'Clinical Trial'), copied as reported; not interpreted
publication_types.title: Publication Types

source_id.description: the source's own identifier, e.g. a PMID or NCT number -- never fabricated
source_id.title: Source Id

RankingResponse.description:
The candidate-ranking response shape. ``model_status`` is
``"ready"`` only when a precomputed serving bundle
(``repurposemap.serving``) exists for the requested disease --
never a live model inference result today, and never silently
substituted with a mock or random ranking otherwise.

``serving_mode`` makes the provenance of a ``"ready"`` response
explicit: ``"precomputed"`` means every candidate here came from an
on-disk ``CandidateRankingBundle`` exported by
``repurposemap.serving.export_rankings`` from an already-approved
ranking output, not from inference run during this request.

candidate_universe.description: what set of drugs the ranking was computed over -- set only when serving_mode is 'precomputed'
candidate_universe.title: Candidate Universe

disclaimer.default: Research hypothesis ranking. Not a treatment recommendation.
disclaimer.title: Disclaimer

generated_at.description: when the precomputed bundle was generated -- set only when serving_mode is 'precomputed'
generated_at.title: Generated At

ranking_method.description: e.g. 'path_quality', 'transe', 'rgcn' -- set only when serving_mode is 'precomputed'
ranking_method.title: Ranking Method

RankingResponse.title: RankingResponse

SafetyEvidence.description:
One raw safety signal from DailyMed/openFDA, before it is
distilled into an API-facing ``repurposemap.api.schemas.SafetyFlag``.
Never a dosing recommendation or clinical judgment, never a safety
score, and never an inferred contraindication beyond what the
source's own label text says -- a pointer to a real external record
only.

adverse_event_context.description: the label's own adverse_reactions text, copied as reported, when the source provides it
adverse_event_context.title: Adverse Event Context

boxed_warning_present.description: true only if the label's own boxed_warning section was non-empty
boxed_warning_present.title: Boxed Warning Present

contraindication_text.description: the label's own contraindications text, copied as reported
contraindication_text.title: Contraindication Text

description.description: a human-readable summary of whichever section below was found, kept for backward compatibility
description.title: Description

drug_name.description: the query drug name this record was retrieved for
drug_name.title: Drug Name

warning_text.description: the label's own warnings/warnings_and_cautions text, copied as reported
warning_text.title: Warning Text

SafetyEvidence.title: SafetyEvidence

SafetyFlag.description:
A caution attached to a candidate -- e.g. a known contraindication
or interaction. Structural placeholder: no safety-data source is wired
up yet, so this is never populated with invented content.
SafetyFlag.title: SafetyFlag

SourceLookupStatus.description:
Whether one of the four evidence/safety sources answered this
request. A source that failed is reported here with its error, never
silently folded into an empty-but-successful result -- see
``repurposemap.evidence``'s own "never swallowed into an empty result"
rule, which this endpoint preserves rather than hides from the caller.

error.description: set only when succeeded is False
error.title: Error

SourceLookupStatus.title: SourceLookupStatus

SupportedDiseaseSummary.description:
One disease a precomputed ranking serving bundle exists for
today. Lets the frontend know in advance what ``POST /api/v1/rank``
can actually answer, instead of discovering it one failed query at
a time.
SupportedDiseaseSummary.title: SupportedDiseaseSummary

SupportedDiseasesResponse.description:
What ``GET /api/v1/rank/diseases`` returns: every disease with a
valid serving bundle under ``data/serving/`` right now. An empty
list is an honest, expected answer -- not an error -- until a real
ranking output has been approved and exported.
SupportedDiseasesResponse.title: SupportedDiseasesResponse

TargetAssociation.description:
One gene/protein target associated with the disease, with Open
Targets' own evidence-integration scores. ``genetic_association_score``
is ``None`` when Open Targets has no genetic-evidence datatype score
for this target/disease pair -- never defaulted to 0, which would
read as "evidence against" rather than "no genetic evidence datatype
scored".

genetic_association_score.description: the 'genetic_association' datatype score (0-1), if Open Targets reports one
genetic_association_score.title: Genetic Association Score

overall_score.description: Open Targets' overall association score (0-1), across all datatypes
overall_score.title: Overall Score

TargetAssociation.title: TargetAssociation

TargetMatch.description:
One candidate target returned when resolving a free-text gene
symbol to an Open Targets target ID (Ensembl).

search_score.description: Open Targets' own search relevance score, not a biological score
search_score.title: Search Score

TargetMatch.title: TargetMatch

TargetScorecard.description:
What Open Targets reports for one target in isolation (no
disease context): tractability, Open Targets' own target
prioritisation factors, and the tissues where it is most highly
expressed. ``prioritisation_factors`` keeps Open Targets' own factor
names (e.g. ``geneticConstraint``, ``mouseKOScore``,
``tissueSpecificity``) as keys -- see the Open Targets documentation
for what each one means; this never re-labels or re-scores them.
TargetScorecard.title: TargetScorecard

TargetScorecardQuery.description:
A request to look up the target scorecard for one gene/protein
target (PLAN.md researcher workflow step 2: "Which proteins are
worth hitting?"). Exactly one of ``gene_symbol``/``ensembl_id``
should be given -- ``gene_symbol`` is resolved to an Open Targets
(Ensembl) ID first (see ``TargetScorecardResponse.resolved_from``);
``ensembl_id`` skips that resolution step.
TargetScorecardQuery.title: TargetScorecardQuery

TargetScorecardResponse.description:
What ``POST /api/v1/target-scorecard`` returns. ``resolved_from``
is set only when ``gene_symbol`` was given and had to be resolved to
an Ensembl ID first.

disclaimer.default: Research evidence integration from Open Targets. Tractability is not a guarantee a drug can be developed.
disclaimer.title: Disclaimer

TargetScorecardResponse.title: TargetScorecardResponse

TissueExpression.description:
The target's expression level in one tissue, from Open Targets'
baseline expression data (Expression Atlas / HPA / GTEx, as Open
Targets integrates them). ``median`` is ``None`` when Open Targets
reports no quantified value for this tissue/unit pair -- never
defaulted to 0, which would read as "not expressed" rather than
"not quantified".
TissueExpression.title: TissueExpression

TractabilityAssessment.description:
One tractability criterion Open Targets checked for a target --
e.g. whether it has an approved drug, a druggable pocket, or a
high-quality ligand, for a given drug modality (small molecule,
antibody, PROTAC, other). ``value`` is the criterion's own
true/false result, not a composite score.
TractabilityAssessment.title: TractabilityAssessment

info.description: Explainable drug-repurposing research API. Every ranking output is a research hypothesis for expert review, never a treatment recommendation.
info.title: RepurposeMap API
